question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that $121,{c}^{2},$ and ${d}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{121{c}^{2}{d}^{2}} & =\sqrt{{11}^{2}\cdot {c}^{2}\cdot {d}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{11\cdot 11\cdot c\cdot c\cdot d\cdot d} \\  & =\sqrt{11\cdot c\cdot d\cdot 11\cdot c\cdot d} \\  & =\sqrt{(11cd)\cdot (11cd)} \\  & =\sqrt{(11cd)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(11cd)^{2}} & =|11cd| \\  & =|11|\cdot |cd| \\  & =11|cd|\end{aligned}
$$
